description: This pie chart visually represents the distribution of media sources across different categories, likely indicating their relative influence or presence within a specific dataset, with each slice corresponding to a distinct outlet or group. The chart is divided into 16 distinct slices, each labeled with the name of a media entity or category. The largest slice, colored dark blue, represents “Breitbart” and accounts for 14% of the total. The second largest, a gray slice labeled “Other,” makes up 13%. “Drudge Report” is shown in orange at 8%, and “The Daily Caller” in green also at 8%. “NPR” (red) and “The Huffington Post” (purple) each represent 7% and 6% respectively. “Vox” (brown) and “The Guardian” (pink) are both at 6% and 5%. “BBC” (gray) and “RT” (yellow) are each at 5% and 4%. The smallest segments, each labeled “Daily Kos,” “National Review,” “Mail,” “Red State,” “Fox News,” “CNN,” “PoliticoUSA,” and “Shareblue,” are all shown as 3% slices. The chart includes a legend that matches each label to its color, and percentage values are printed directly inside each slice. The slices are arranged in a clockwise order, generally from largest to smallest, though not perfectly sorted.
